title: sprintgate-readiness-heuristics-and-latency-budget
summary: Compact readiness canvas combining a week-by-week sprint gate checklist, KPI guardrails and a simple latency budget calculator tailored for Redwood inference launches (hosted/dedicated/private). Focused on ops heuristics and quick go/no-go thresholds.
content:
Purpose:
- One-page working sheet to align product-ops, serving-runtime, SRE and solutions on go/no-go signals for SprintGate (final 14 days before traffic launch).
- Emphasis: measurable KPIs, automated smoke probes, and clear rollback triggers for latency, errors, cost, and quality regressions.

Scope:
- Applies to feature rollouts that touch inference surface (API behavior changes, model swaps, routing policies, cache changes, batching tweaks).
- Covers hosted + dedicated + private variants; notes highlight differences where needed.

Quick read: TL;DR guardrails (set realistic for initial beta):
- Customer-facing p95 latency (gen) <= 800ms, p99 <= 2s for 8k token sequences under normal load
- Error rate (5xx) <= 0.2% sustained, spike tolerance 0.5% for <= 15m
- Token cost delta vs baseline <= +25% for model upgrade OR measurable quality lift (NPS or eval metric)
- Throughput (tokens/s per GPU) must meet demand curve at target concurrency with <10% queuing

14-day prelaunch cadence (high level):
- D-14: Finalize model artifact + quantization profile, lock rollout policy, sign-off on owner list
- D-10: Smoke tests (unit-level): kernel selection, KV cache correctness, logging hooks verified
- D-7: Load test parity run (simulate expected traffic + 50%), validate latency SLO and autoscale behavior
- D-3: Canary at 1% traffic; watch quality evals and token cost; run rollback drill
- D-1: Increase to 10% (if canary healthy) and run chaos scenarios (AZ fail, GPU OOM injection)
- Launch day: Phased ramp + on-call rotations + pre-authorized rollback criteria

KPI tracker (single-row compact format for daily update):
- Metric: current_value | threshold | trend | owner | notes
- p95 latency (generate): "720ms" | "<=800ms" | "flat" | "Leah Kim" | "batching adjusted on D-8"
- p99 latency: "1.8s" | "<=2s" | "down" | "Leah Kim" | "saw 300ms improvement after kernel tweak"
- 5xx error rate: "0.12%" | "<=0.2%" | "up" | "Diego Morales" | "spike coincided with cache invalidation"
- Token cost delta (1M tokens): "+12%" | "<=25%" | "flat" | "Arjun Patel" | "quantization helps but increases latency slightly"
- Throughput headroom: "+18%" | ">=+15%" | "flat" | "SRE oncall" | "autoscale cushion verified"

Latency budget quick calc (shorthand) - used for tradeoffs:
- Input: target end2end p95 budget = 800ms
- Breakdown example (typical): network + api gateway = 100ms, request routing + auth = 40ms, pre/post-processing = 80ms, model inference = 580ms => total 800ms
- If inference engine changes (new model/quant) and inference -> 720ms, then we have only 80ms for overhead. Action: allow batching changes/route bypass or reduce max_seq to preserve p95.
- Heuristic: always keep 10–20% headroom for transient spikes when setting SLOs.

Smoke test matrix (automated probes that must pass before canary):
- Unit probes (fast): model load, kv-cache warm start, tokenization parity, kernel health -> pass
- Integration probes (minutes): end-to-end gen for 10 prompts (short/long/edge tokenization) -> quality threshold: semantic-f1 >= baseline - 2pt
- Load probes (hour): synthetic traffic ramp to 150% expected concurrency -> watch queue length, p99 and OOMs
- Regression probes: run eval suite against golden prompts and compare scoring artifact; alert if delta > target

Canary runbook (short):
- Canary size: start 1% for 30m -> 5% for 60m -> 10% for 2h -> scale based on signals
- Abort triggers (immediate): p95 > threshold for 3 consecutive windows (5m), 5xx rate > 0.5% rolling 15m, eval-quality delta > critical threshold
- Rollback steps: switch routing policy to fallback model variant (pre-tested), revoke canary config, run quick sanity checks. Communicate on #prodops and #incidents.

Cost vs quality decision matrix (simple):
- If cost delta <= +10% and quality uplift >= small (e.g., +1 eval point): accept
- If cost delta between +10% and +25%: require product signoff + A/B revenue/engagement hypothesis
- If cost delta > +25%: require exec review or restrict to dedicated/private customers only

Operational heuristics (notes & gotchas):
- Batching: marginal gains at high QPS but hurts p95 for short prompts; use workload-aware gating (auto-batch on long sequences only).
- KV caching: prefix-heavy workloads -> massive win; ensure cache invalidation strategy obvious in release notes (customer impact if cache key changes).
- Quantization: test for subtle quality regressions (hallucination rate); small eval deltas can compound in production prompts.
- Routing fallbacks: precompute compatibility table of model variants for seamless fallback; store in config repo.

Ownership / Roles quick map (two-line):
- Product-ops: Maya (overall launch conductor), runbook + comms
- Serving-runtime: Leah (latency, kernel workarounds), Arjun (model artifact and quant profiles)
- SRE: Diego (load tests, autoscale, infra rollbacks)
- Solutions/CS: TBD (customer-facing doc + opt-in messaging)

Preflight checklist (checkbox style, notes allowed):
- [ ] Model artifact SHA locked and stored in artifact repo (owner: Arjun)
- [ ] Quant profile + fallback artifact validated (owner: Arjun)
- [ ] Canary route config ready and tested in staging (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Smoke probes automated in CI with green run (owner: Leah)
- [ ] Load test script + target matrix committed (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Cost sensitivity analysis and threshold signed off (owner: Product lead)
- [ ] Public docs / changelog drafted for customers (owner: Solutions)
- [ ] Oncall rotation and escalation sheet published (owner: SRE)

Contingency templates (short snippets to paste into incident):
- Immediate rollback message: "Initiating rollback to model-variant:v2-fallback. Canary aborted at X%. Reason: p95 breach/5xx spike. Eng oncall: @<name>. Investigating - more updates T+15m."
- If autoscale fails: "Switch traffic to secondary region/ Dedicated pool. Notify infra and escalate to SRE manager."

Open questions / follow-ups (notes to self):
- Should we require A/B revenue gating for all cost deltas > 10% or only for hosted API? (action: product decision by D-7)
- Need a concise list of golden prompts for evals across languages (action: ask localization team)
- Add a small script to compute latency budget automatically from measured infra timings (action: SRE + runtime)

Appendix: quick commands & tickets (scratch):
- Load test runner: load-test/runner --profile=canary-150pct --duration=60m
- Key tickets: JIRA OPS-4123 (canary automation), JIRA PERF-1198 (kernel opt), GH PR repo/PR#256 (quant test harness)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this sheet compact; ops folks hate huge playbooks. Use anchors in the final release runbook.
- After launch: convert daily KPI row into automated dashboard widget and remove manual updates.
